rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Water pollution — causes, effects, and control ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Water pollution — causes** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Environmental Issues fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Water pollution is any change in water quality that harms life or usefulness. The big concepts: **BOD** (biochemical oxygen demand — the oxygen microbes need to decompose the waste; high BOD = dirty water), **eutrophication** (nutrient enrichment → algal bloom → oxygen crash), and **biomagnification** (toxics like DDT and mercury climbing the food chain).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Eutrophication chain: nutrient (N, P) enrichment → algal bloom → O2 depletion → fish death → anaerobic decay (foul smell) — the five-step causal chain is the answer.  ·  Trick 2: BOD: oxygen needed by microbes to decompose organic matter — higher BOD = more pollution; clean water BOD < 5 ppm; sewage treatment uses BOD reduction as its goal.

Key terms and statements Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).  ·  **Worked example — reading a BOD test.** Sample A: BOD 5 mg/L, dissolved oxygen 8 mg/L. Sample B: BOD 300 mg/L, dissolved oxygen 2 mg/L. Sample B carries heavy organic pollution — microbes will strip the remaining oxygen, fish will suffocate, and anaerobic decay will produce foul H2S. Sample A is healthy water.…  ·  ## 7. Exam Zone NEB past-question map (long/short), topic-wise MCQs with explanations, and short tricks (block VII). rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Most-asked points (NEB).** (1) Define BOD and explain what a high BOD means. (2) Trace the eutrophication sequence step by step. (3) Explain biomagnification with the DDT-in-bird example. (4) Name the three sewage-treatment stages and what each removes. (5) Why does warm water pollute?  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Water pollution is measured by BOD, amplified by eutrophication and biomagnification, and controlled by staged sewage treatment plus watershed care. **Self-check:** can you order the eutrophication steps and state what happens to DDT concentration at each trophic level?
